`hatch-vcs` built the version from git (`0.0.post1+g3ff5fcaff`, since the clone has no tags — the expected fallback, not an error).

## Compatibility fix

The unpinned install pulled very recent `pytest` 9 / `pytest-asyncio` 1.x, which broke `test_async_other_thread` (event-loop policy interaction — it passed alone but failed in the full run). I pinned to versions compatible with the repo's era/CI:

```bash
pip3 install "pytest<8" "pytest-asyncio==0.23.8" "pytest-benchmark<5" "pytest-rerunfailures<14"
```

## Verification

```
python3 -c "import fsspec"   # imports from /testbed (editable install)
python3 -m pytest fsspec -q   # exit code 0
→ 1385 passed, 330 skipped, 2 xfailed
```

`pip check` reports no broken requirements. The 330 skips are optional backends (s3, gcs, ssh, etc.) whose third-party deps aren't installed; the core and HTTP/local/memory suites all pass.

Setup is complete. Here's what I did:

## Environment setup

The environment started empty (no `python3`, `pip`, `git`, or compilers), so I installed the base toolchain globally via `apt`:

```bash
apt-get update
apt-get install -y python3 python3-pip python3-dev git build-essential
```

## Project setup (fsspec)

Per the README, fsspec is a pure-Python package using the `hatchling` + `hatch-vcs` build backend. I installed it in editable mode with its `test` extra:

```bash
git config --global --add safe.directory /testbed   # fix dubious-ownership
pip3 install -e ".[test]"
```

`hatch-vcs` built the version from git (`0.0.post1+g3ff5fcaff`, since the clone has no tags — the expected fallback, not an error).

## Compatibility fix

The unpinned install pulled very recent `pytest` 9 / `pytest-asyncio` 1.x, which broke `test_async_other_thread` (event-loop policy interaction — it passed alone but failed in the full run). I pinned to versions compatible with the repo's era/CI:

```bash
pip3 install "pytest<8" "pytest-asyncio==0.23.8" "pytest-benchmark<5" "pytest-rerunfailures<14"
```

## Verification

```
python3 -c "import fsspec"   # imports from /testbed (editable install)
python3 -m pytest fsspec -q   # exit code 0
→ 1385 passed, 330 skipped, 2 xfailed
```

`pip check` reports no broken requirements. The 330 skips are optional backends (s3, gcs, ssh, etc.) whose third-party deps aren't installed; the core and HTTP/local/memory suites all pass.
